title: Arrival
scope: The 2016 film · Louise’s changing experience of time
premise: Louise sees scenes with a daughter before we understand where they belong in her life. How does seeing her future help her during the visitors’ arrival?
ending: Louise’s experience of time includes her future with Ian and their daughter Hannah. Information from a future encounter helps her act in the present; the family scenes are not simply an earlier chapter of her life.

people.name: Louise Banks
people.introduction: A linguist learning a language that changes how she experiences time.

events.title: Family scenes appear without their place in time
events.text: The film shows Louise with a daughter. At first, these scenes invite us to understand them as recollections. Their position in Louise’s life is the central reveal.
events.whenLabel: As the film first presents them

events.title: Louise begins learning the visitors’ language
events.text: Louise, a linguist, works with physicist Ian Donnelly to communicate with the alien visitors, the heptapods. As she learns their language, she experiences scenes from her own future.

events.title: She recognises a future, not a lost past
events.text: The girl is Hannah, the daughter Louise will have with Ian. The family scenes show a life still ahead of Louise during the arrival.

events.title: A future conversation contains what she needs now
events.text: During the crisis, Louise experiences a future reception with General Shang, a Chinese military leader. At that later meeting, he tells her what she said in the phone call that changed his decision.
events.whenLabel: A later reception, experienced during the crisis

events.title: She uses that information to make the call
events.text: Louise calls Shang during the crisis. She repeats his wife’s dying words, learned through their future encounter, and helps persuade him to call off the attack on the visitors.

events.title: She accepts the life she has glimpsed
events.text: Knowing the joy and loss ahead, Louise embraces a life with Ian and their daughter Hannah. Her knowledge of that future is part of the decision she makes as the arrival ends.
events.whenLabel: As the arrival ends · with knowledge of the future

chapters.title: Reconsider the apparent memories
chapters.introduction: Begin with what the film shows us, then reconsider it with Louise. Seeing a moment and living through its events can happen at different points in her life.

chapters.title: See how future knowledge acts now

sources.title: Repository story record
sources.note: Editorial pilot adapted from the repository. Scene wording and interpretation await a separate review against the primary work.

sources.title: Eric Heisserer on the opening, Shang’s words and Louise’s choice
sources.note: Julian Blythe’s 4 December 2016 interview with the screenwriter. Relevant answers concern the Mandarin line, the daughter’s illness and writing the film’s order. This supports those elements, not every detail of the reception or a complete theory of free will.

connections.label: Words learned at the later meeting enable Louise’s earlier phone call.
